manual: Instructions for the Experiment: Pyrolytic Graphite Hovering Above a Neodymium Magnet ArrayI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Pyrolytic Graphite Diamagnetic Levitation2. Subject: Engineering - Electrical Engineering (Electromagnetics)3. Experiment Objective: To demonstrate diamagnetism and magnetic field shaping by observing stable hovering of pyrolytic graphite above a checkerboard array of neodymium magnets; to practice precise setup and visual documentation via time-lapse.II. Experimental Equipment- Neodymium cube magnets (e.g., 5–10 mm, 16–36 pieces)- Non-magnetic base plate (plastic/acrylic)- Thin square of pyrolytic graphite (≈20–30 mm, <0.5 mm thick)- Tweezers (non-magnetic)- Camera or smartphone with tripod- Flat tabletopIII. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Place the non-magnetic base on a flat tabletop. Ensure the surface is level and vibration-free.2. Magnet Arrangement: Arrange the cube magnets into a checkerboard grid with alternating north/south poles facing upward. Press magnets tightly together to minimize gaps.3. Camera Setup: Mount the camera above or at a shallow angle to the array. Fix focus and exposure; enable time-lapse or continuous recording.4. Core Operation: Using tweezers, gently lower the pyrolytic graphite to a few millimeters above the magnet array center, then release without imparting lateral force.5. Observation Period: Allow the graphite to settle. Record the hovering and any small lateral stabilization over the array.6. Completion: Stop recording. Carefully remove the graphite and disassemble magnets for storage.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: Graphite is unsupported above the array.2. After Release: The graphite rises slightly or remains suspended, hovering a small distance above the magnets.3. Stabilization: The graphite shows lateral confinement near the array center, with small oscillations that damp out.V. Summary of Experimental PrinciplesPyrolytic graphite is strongly diamagnetic, generating an induced magnetic moment opposite to the applied magnetic field. The checkerboard magnet array creates a strong field gradient. The diamagnetic repulsion balances gravity, enabling stable levitation. Spatial field variation provides lateral trapping, resulting in a stable hovering equilibrium.VI. Experimental Precautions- Handle neodymium magnets carefully to avoid pinching.- Use non-magnetic tools.- Avoid air currents and vibrations for stable hovering.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Diamagnetic levitation of pyrolytic graphite in a shaped magnetic field. Minimum assumptions: graphite is thin and diamagnetic; magnet array has alternating poles creating strong gradients; gravity is balanced by magnetic repulsion.Phased storyline: (1) Static setup on tabletop with checkerboard magnet array; (2) camera fixed and focused; (3) graphite lowered and released; (4) immediate vertical balance and visible hovering; (5) brief lateral stabilization with small oscillations. Visibility constraints: clear view of gap between graphite and magnets; stable framing to verify hovering and confinement.
